epic.name: Sign-in and App Shell
unverifiedAssumptions: Verify signing in actually keeps you signed in: the app assumes the session cookie the back end sets still works when it passes through the front end's same-address forwarding, which depends on the cookie's settings in local development without https. If it doesn't, sign-in will look successful and then bounce you straight back to the sign-in screen.

Verify the menu and landing screen match your role: the app assumes the back end reports the role spelled exactly 'Importer' or 'Approver', alongside your name and email. If the wording or field differs, you may land on the wrong screen or see an empty or wrong menu.

Verify being signed out elsewhere sends you to sign-in: the app assumes the back end answers a timed-out or replaced session with a plain 'not signed in' reply. If it answers differently, the first browser may show an error message instead of returning you to sign-in.

Verify signing in through the app reaches the real back end: the front end forwards everything under /api/ to http://localhost:8042/api/ unchanged. With the back end running and mock mode off, signing in should work end to end.
Check the connection-problem wording is OK: "We can't reach the app right now. Check your connection and try again."
Confirm the app name: the header and browser tab say 'Transaction Import'. Tell me if you prefer a different product name.
Check the signed-out message wording: 'You've been signed out. This happens after 60 minutes without activity or when you sign in somewhere else. Please sign in again.'
Check the no-access wording: 'You don't have access to this screen' / 'If you need to use it, ask your administrator to change your role.'
Warning messages are treated like problems (they stay until closed), not like success messages (which fade). Is that right?
